text:
maria: Heads up — followed the tarball install guide on WSL2 and seeing a weird combo: `redwoodctl` runs, but `redwoodctl login` errors with `config not found` and `redwoodctl local serve` fails with `bind: permission denied` on /run/redwood.sock. Anyone seen this?
jon: Oof. Did you extract with sudo? That tends to make the binary and config dirs owned by root.
maria: Yep did `sudo tar -xzf redwoodctl-linux.tar.gz -C /usr/local/bin`. `which redwoodctl` -> `/usr/local/bin/redwoodctl` and `ls -l` shows root:root. The login error mentions `~/.config/redwood` missing but I do have an old `~/.redwood` from a previous version.
alan: Try `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$HOME/.redwood redwoodctl login` or move it `mv ~/.redwood ~/.config/redwood`. Newer CLI uses XDG. Also check `chmod +x /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl` and `chown $(whoami) /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl` if you used sudo.
maria: Moved the folder. `redwoodctl login` now wants the browser flow but in WSL headless I usually do `redwoodctl login --headless` — that fails with `failed to write token: permission denied`.
jon: Where is it trying to write the token? Older CLIs wrote to `/tmp/redwood_token_$USER` in our CI, the new one writes to `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/token` and will fail if that dir is root-owned. Maybe check `ls -la ~/.config/redwood`.
devex-bot: Reminder: run `redwoodctl version` and report if < v0.8.0 — there was a breaking config path change in v0.8.0.
maria: `redwoodctl version` -> v0.9.2. `~/.config/redwood` is root:root because earlier I did `sudo mv` — doh. `sudo chown -R $(id -u):$(id -g) ~/.config/redwood` fixed the token write. But `redwoodctl local serve` still errors: `listen unix /run/redwood.sock: bind: permission denied`.
alan: On WSL `/run` is root-owned and user processes can't bind there unless elevated. We changed the default socket path to `/run/redwood.sock` for system installs but for user installs we ought to fallback to `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/redwood.sock`. Check `echo $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`.
maria: `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is empty. I did `export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/tmp/runtime-$USER` and restarted shell, then `redwoodctl local serve --socket $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/redwood.sock` works. Is that intended? Feels like a bad default on WSL.
jon: Agreed. We should detect WSL and fallback to `~/.cache/redwood/runtime.sock` or similar. Filing a bug/PR?
alan: Filed DEVEX-4281 — add WSL/runtime fallback + clearer install docs. Also adding a `redwoodctl doctor` check to warn about root-owned config dirs.
maria: :thumbsup: Thanks. For posterity, steps that fixed my setup:
```
sudo chown -R $(id -u):$(id -g) ~/.config/redwood
export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/tmp/runtime-$(id -u)
redwoodctl local serve --socket $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/redwood.sock
redwoodctl login --headless
```
devex-bot: Ticket DEVEX-4281 created and linked to PR #8790. If anyone wants to pick up the `--wsl-fallback` patch ping @jon.
